name: What pool shape works best for a view lot in Glendale or Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Which pool design is best when the property has a city, canyon, or mountain view?
mainEntity.text: Which pool design is best when the property has a city, canyon, or mountain view?

acceptedAnswer.text: On view lots, the pool should frame the scenery rather than compete with it. Long rectangular or geometric designs often work best because they create strong sightlines and can be oriented toward a canyon, skyline, or mountain view. On hillside properties, an infinity edge or raised terrace can enhance the visual effect, but only if the design supports the view direction and the structural conditions. The home’s interior views matter too, because the pool should look good from living areas and not just from the backyard. The best design usually keeps the composition simple so the view remains the star. Homeowners should ask the designer how the pool will read from inside the house, at night, and from key outdoor seating areas. A view lot is often less about pool size and more about placement and proportion.
acceptedAnswer.description: View lots often work best with long, clean pool lines and an edge or orientation that highlights the view. The pool should be placed to preserve sightlines from the home and create a strong visual connection to the landscape.
